title: Annotatio II §.V open: Burmann & Bayer name Paschasius Radbertus first Consubstantiation author
pass_a_gloss: §. V. There are indeed, both from the Reformed Francis Burmann (Synopsis of Theology Tom. 2 p. 401) and from the Lutherans Joh. Wilhelm Bayer (Historical Theology p. 593), who at that time constitute PASCHASIUS RADBERTUS, Abbot of Corbie, Bertram’s coeval adversary, in a book of the same name as Bertram’s book, the first Author and Father of Consubstantiation.
pass_b_english: §.V: Reformed Burmann (Synopsis Theol. II p. 401) and Lutheran Bayer (Theol. Histor. p. 593) both cast Paschasius Radbertus, Abbot of Corbie — Bertram’s coeval adversary — as Consubstantiation’s first author and father.
They point to his book under the same title as Bertram’s.
source_text: §. V. Enimverò sunt, tàm ex Reformatis Franciscus Burmannus, Synops. Theol. Tom. 2. p. 401. quàm ex Lutheranis, Joh. Wilhelm. Bajerus, Theol. Histor. p. 593. qui illo tempore PASCHASIUM RHADEBERTUM, Abbatem Corbeiensem, Bertrami adversarium Coævum, in libro ejusdem cum Bertrami libro nominis, primum Consubstantiationis Autorem Patremque constituunt.
notes: §.V open; Burmann/Bayer name Paschasius first author.
